hero.body: Fabric is an open, non-profit foundation that publishes and governs interoperability standards for digital payments — covering everything from stablecoin settlement to privacy-preserving cash instruments.

strip.p1_desc: Any bank, any wallet, any network — Fabric standards are designed to work across all of them without proprietary lock-in.
strip.p2_desc: Every standard published by the foundation is built around verifiable, cryptographic guarantees. No black boxes.
strip.p3_desc: No venture capital, no exit, no pivot. The foundation exists solely to publish and maintain open standards.

how.intro: Stablecoins are already used at scale for payments worldwide. SSF-001 provides the missing layer: a common open standard for how those payments are initiated, authorised, settled, and confirmed — across wallets, merchants, and acquirers.
how.s1_desc: The merchant server requests a charge session and redirects the user to the payment processor's secure checkout (Stablecoin Stack conformant)
how.s2_desc: The payer scans a QRCode with the conformant wallet or paste the charge's ephemeral id. The wallet exchanges the ephemeral token per the charge's details and produces the cryptographic artifacts.
how.s3_desc: The wallet submits the cryptographic artifacts to the Payment Processor.
how.s4_desc: The payment processor broadcasts the cryptographic artifacts, awaits for on-chain validation and replies to the merchant.

cashpack.body1: Every digital payment today exposes the sender, receiver, amount, and timestamp to the network — by design. CashPack changes that. It defines a signed, transferable digital instrument — the cash-pack — that passes between parties, without the intermediate paties being identified. Only the Edges are.
cashpack.body2: Structurally analogous to physical banknotes: the Operator sees who locked funds and who redeemed them. The intermediate chain is visible only to its participants — with cryptographic verification at every step and a tamper-evident audit trail available to authorised investigators.
cashpack.h1_desc: Works with core banking, tokenized deposits, permissioned ledgers, or public blockchains — the Operator chooses.
cashpack.h2_desc: Intermediate transfers stay private. Authorised investigators retain access to a tamper-evident audit trail.
cashpack.h3_desc: Generalises to vouchers, gift instruments, tokenized deposits, digital securities, and bearer bonds.
cashpack.flow_s1_desc: The Principal asks the Operator to lock a specific amount. A signed cash-pack is issued, addressed to the first recipient's public key.
cashpack.flow_s2_desc: Holder passes to the CashPack (digital file) to next holder
cashpack.flow_s3_desc: The final holder presents the instrument to the Operator. The cryptographic chain is verified, and funds are released.

community.body: Fabric standards are shaped by the people and institutions that use them. There are several ways to participate — from reading a draft to contributing to the next version of a specification.
community.c1_desc: Ask questions about any specification, propose ideas, or report ambiguities. A public space for implementation-level discussion with the broader community and core contributors.
community.c2_desc: Structured groups that draft, review, and ratify changes to each specification. Open to any individual or institution. Working group meetings are public and recorded.
community.c3_desc: All specification sources, reference implementations, test vectors, and tooling — in the open. File issues, submit pull requests, or simply follow along.

contributors.title: People who build the standards.
contributors.banner_desc: All Fabric standards are developed in the open. Whether you're fixing a typo in a spec or proposing a new message type, contributions of all sizes are welcome.

sponsors.body: The foundation is funded entirely by its member institutions and sponsors — no advertising, no data monetisation, no external investors. Sponsorship is how open payment standards stay independent.
sponsors.s1_desc: A leading European retail bank and co-author of the original Stablecoin Stack messaging specification.
sponsors.s2_desc: A pan-regional acquirer running production integrations across multiple Fabric standards.
sponsors.s3_desc: An open-banking infrastructure provider and contributor to the cryptographic proof layer.
sponsors.cta_desc: Membership gives your organisation a seat at the governance table, early access to specification drafts, and attribution across foundation materials. Sponsorship is available at any level.

roles.body: Fabric standards serve every participant in the payments landscape. Find your role and see which specifications are relevant to you.
roles.path1_sub: I run a business and want to accept digital payments
roles.path1_li2: Present a QR code or link — any compatible wallet can pay
roles.path2_sub: I want to send payments using open, interoperable rails
roles.path2_li1: Use any wallet compatible with Fabric standards
roles.path2_li2: Authorise payments without sharing credentials with merchants
roles.path2_li3: Receive a cryptographic receipt on completion
roles.path3_sub: I build financial products and want open, standard building blocks
roles.path3_li1: Embed standards-compliant payment flows in your product
roles.path3_li2: Use open SDKs without proprietary licensing constraints
roles.path3_li3: Interoperate with any institution implementing the same standards
roles.path4_sub: I settle obligations between institutions across borders
roles.path4_li1: Review cross-border message formats across relevant specifications
roles.path4_li2: Align with ISO 20022-compatible flows where applicable
roles.path5_sub: I supervise payment systems and set compliance frameworks
roles.path5_li1: Review the governance model and audit trail design for each standard
roles.path5_li2: Understand how compliance obligations are defined per specification
roles.path6_sub: I study payment systems, cryptography, or financial infrastructure
roles.path6_li1: Access formal specifications and test vectors
roles.path6_li2: Cite and build on openly licensed standards
roles.path7_sub: I implement, integrate, or extend systems based on open standards
roles.path7_li1: Use reference implementations as a validated starting point
roles.path7_li2: Run the test environment locally in minutes

about.body1: The Fabric Payment Standards Foundation is a neutral, non-profit organisation that publishes and governs open standards for digital payments. It was created by its member institutions — not by a startup looking to own a network.
about.body2: No company owns any Fabric standard. No vendor controls them. All specifications are public, all reference implementations are open source, and anyone can integrate, audit, or build on them.
about.body3: Governance decisions are made by the member council. The foundation's only mandate is to keep its standards open, stable, and interoperable — for as long as they are needed.
about.p4: Built to last, not to trend
